concept: A flat-cosmos night world with four held stations, each changing state on the spoken word instead of being redrawn. The orbit picture (Earth, tilted rings, satellites broadcasting) says what is overhead. The sky diagram (a cross-section: Earth's curved surface along the bottom, the phone as a glowing point on it, satellites above) is the lesson's working machine: a stamped pulse travels down, a range line becomes a circle, circles meet, swell together when the phone's clock is off, and snap back to one point when a fourth satellite fixes the clock; it returns for the recap. The two-clocks pair (a clock in orbit above, a clock on the ground below, Earth between) shows quartz against atomic, then speed and gravity pulling the orbit clock's rate, then the clock set slow before launch. The night city with the blue dot opens and closes the film, carries the 300 metre ruler, drifts 10 km in a day and comes home.

story.metaphor: None: the literal system, drawn flat. Earth, satellites, a signal, circles, clocks, a phone and its blue dot.
story.setting: One night field: the city below, Earth and its satellites above, a cross-section diagram, and two clocks.
story.arc: A blue dot appears on a night map; the answer is overhead: satellites with atomic clocks broadcasting where and when; travel time gives a distance, a distance gives a sphere, spheres meet at you; the phone's cheap clock breaks it and a fourth satellite fixes it; the satellites' own clocks run fast in orbit and are set slow before launch; the chain replays and the dot lands.

devices.what: The ranging cross-section held from b08 to b24 and replayed in b31 and b32: Earth's curved surface across the bottom with the phone as a glowing teal point, satellites above, a stamped pulse, range lines that sweep into circles (spheres drawn as circles), the overlap ring, two candidate points, all circles swelling together and snapping back to one point.

The one join material: camera moves between the four stations of the one night world (up from the city to orbit, across to the diagram, on to the clocks), continue joins inside a station, hard cuts only at the open and into the recap.

value_script.why: a lift at the close: the city lights brighten

parts.what: The viewer's phone, flat: rounded body in shadow with a surface bezel, crescent shading, offset shadow. Screen states: dark, map (a simplified night map like the city plan), dot (the blue dot in accent4 with a soft pulse ring, offset parameter so it can drift and come home), halo (a soft accent4 uncertainty disc round the dot, size parameter). A readout form for the diagram: a rounded panel (about 500 x 260) that shows a running timer (counts to a given value and stops), and up to four short label rows that light in turn. A quartz clock form: a small cheap clock face that sits on the phone. A mini form (about 280 x 480) for insets. Never a hand or a person.

Earth, flat-cosmos: a crescent-shaded disc (oceans in surface, land in accent4 at low saturation, the night side in shadow with a few warm city lights) with an optional glowing accent4 point for the phone's place, at any radius. An arc form: the curved surface seen from close, spanning the frame bottom, with the phone point on its crest. A gravity well form: curved grid lines dipping under Earth, deep near the surface and shallowing with height, with a height marker that can slide up the well.

A GPS satellite, flat: a box body in surface with crescent shading, two solar panels in field2 with accent2 cell lines, an antenna dish facing Earth, and a small clock face slot on its body. States: idle (muted), named (body edge in accent while spoken), dim, broadcasting (rings pulse out from the antenna at a steady rate), on_rocket (seated on a small two-stage rocket for the launch, with a flame that can fire). Sizes from a 24 px point in the constellation to a 360 px close-up.

Signals: a travelling pulse (a short bright arc of wavefront in accent2 with a soft glow) that moves from a point to a point at a given progress, with up to two riding chips (a position pin chip, a time stamp chip with a tiny clock); concentric broadcast rings; a light beam streak (a long thin accent2 line with a bright head) for the speed of light; a bent path (refracts slightly crossing a band) and a bounce path (reflects off an anchor).

The ranging machinery of the cross-section: a range line from a satellite to a point (label anchor at its middle); a circle around a satellite through a point, drawn by the range line sweeping round, with a radius offset parameter so every circle can swell or shrink together by the same amount; the overlap ring of two circles drawn as a thin tilted ellipse through their two crossing points (a sphere-meets-sphere ring in the flat picture); candidate point markers (bright accent2 discs that can dim or glow); a blurred patch where swollen circles no longer meet (a soft neg tinted region); a snap to one point. Circles in line at mid opacity, the one named in accent.

A flat clock face (ink face ring, surface fill, crescent shading) whose hands are driven by time with a rate and an offset parameter: steady, off (an offset it cannot know), behind, ahead, in_step, and set_slow (a small knob on its rim turns back). A microsecond chip slot beside it. Small form (about 60 px) for tags and badges, large form (about 280 px) for the clocks station. Atomic and quartz differ by finish (atomic: a fine ring of tick marks; quartz: plain, a slight wobble), never by a logo.

kit.notes: No people, no hands, no faces anywhere (the brief: people only with a designed flat-cosmos character kit; none is declared). Flat-cosmos tokens only: field and field2 for the night, surface and surface2 for bodies, ink for type, muted and line for quiet parts, accent (orange) for the one element the narration names, accent2 (gold) for signals and light, accent4 (teal) only for the blue dot and the phone's point on Earth (its identity colour throughout), neg only for errors (the patch, the drift). Crescent shading, radius 26 on cards, stroke 4, offset shadow. Type: labels 24 to 30, body 30 to 36. Every on-screen word is the script's on_screen text, nothing else. Numbers only as the script states them.

scenes.subject: The phone only listens; nothing goes up

design.treatment: The cross-section settles: Earth's curved surface across the bottom, the teal phone point on its crest, three satellites above. Signals arrive at the point from all three. An arrow starts to draw upward from the point, stops, and fades out, struck through: nothing leaves.
design.why_motion: the arrow that never completes is the refutation
references: flat-cosmos pack: neg only for errors

design.treatment: In the readout three rows light in turn, each in accent while spoken: arrival (the phone's time), sending (the stamp chip slides into this row), x speed of light; the timer value between them shows the travel time, and a thin line extends from the readout up towards satellite A as the product forms.
design.why_motion: three operations in order; each lands on its word

design.why_motion: the hidden assumption is shown, then broken
